svg.title: where λ = (lm)q ∈C and lm ≥2 is the integer block size at this step. This λ is a scalar multiplying every coefficient in the degree-q fusion; it is not an arbitrary linear change of frame. Since q ≥0, |λ| = lq m ≥1 and |λ−1| = l−q m ≤1, with both moduli equal to one for q = 0; equivalently, scalar multiplication by λ−1 has operator norm at most one on the coefficient space. Thus the first smallness expression is 1/x ≤1 and the second is |λ−1|/4 ≤1/4. A lower bound on the norm of a general operator would not imply this inverse bound; the scalar identity is what proves it here. In the lift the coefficient space is unchanged and λ acts by the same scalar on realized coefficients, so the substitution bound is recovered with the same constants; the inverse bound depends on the homogeneity of the fusion in one degree and would not survive mixing degrees.
